title: Blueprint: Terraform module for internal ingress with controlled TLS handoff and graceful session eviction
creator: Aisha Morgan
description: We need a production-ready Terraform module that standardizes internal ingress within customer VPCs: NLB for L4 pass-through where required, ALB for TLS termination and path-based routing. The module must support a controlled TLS handoff pattern (optionally terminate TLS at ALB or pass-through to target), session eviction/draining hooks, and safe upgrade paths for module consumers (canary upgrades, traffic shifting). It should expose health probe configuration, connection draining timeouts, and a consistent tagging/iam pattern for auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes flags: enable_tls_termination (bool), use_nlb_pass_through (bool), connection_draining_seconds (int)
Can perform a zero-downtime module upgrade using a phased rollout (canary ALB target group replacement + weighted shift) documented in README
Health checks are configurable per-target-group with jittered probe intervals to avoid thundering herd
Automated smoke tests validate both pass-through and TLS-terminated modes in a staging VPC
Observability: CloudWatch/Datadog exportable metrics for unhealthy_host_count, target_response_time, connection_drain_events
implementation_plan: Create module skeleton with submodules: lb_nlb, lb_alb, target_groups, dns, cert_manager
Define inputs/outputs with strict typing and defaults; minimize provider-specific assumptions
Implement optional TLS handoff: route 443 to ALB vs preserve TCP on NLB based on use_nlb_pass_through
Add lifecycle hooks and local-exec null_resource to emit events to a rollout dashboard during upgrades
Create test harness: terraform apply in ephemeral account, run k8s service smoke tests, verify connection draining behavior
Publish example: vpc + two-node ASG + ingress module demonstration in examples/ with upgrade scenario
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Morgan: Initial spike completed. Two feasible approaches: (A) single ALB per environment with path-based routing; (B) hybrid NLB for TCP passthrough + ALB for TLS termination. Hybrid preferred for strict-customer-isolation use-cases.
